text: The sequent calculus has a 'right ∀' rule that says: to prove ∀x.A(x) on the right, you introduce:
choices: a specific witness t and prove A(t)
a fresh variable y not in any hypothesis and prove A(y) on the right
two proofs: one with x=0 and one for x+1
explanation: R∀: Γ ⊢ Δ, A(y) where y is fresh (an eigenvariable). This is the universal generalisation rule for sequents.
